questions.stem: In aerobic respiration, oxygen is required most directly because it:
options: Accepts electrons at the end of the transport chain
Carries ATP into the nucleus
Splits glucose during glycolysis
Converts pyruvate into glucose
questions.explanation: Oxygen accepts electrons and protons at the end of the electron-transport chain, allowing electron flow and oxidative phosphorylation to continue.

questions.stem: A cell temporarily loses functional mitochondria but retains an intact cytosol. Which process can still produce a small amount of ATP?
options: Krebs cycle
Glycolysis
Oxidative phosphorylation
Link reaction
questions.explanation: Glycolysis occurs in the cytosol and produces ATP by substrate-level phosphorylation without requiring mitochondria.

questions.stem: The inner mitochondrial membrane suddenly becomes freely permeable to protons. Which event is affected most directly?
options: DNA transcription in the nucleus
Glucose entry into glycolysis
ATP synthesis by chemiosmosis
Peptide-bond formation on ribosomes
questions.explanation: ATP synthase depends on proton flow down an electrochemical gradient. A proton-permeable membrane collapses that gradient.

questions.stem: A mitochondrial uncoupler increases proton leakage. Which combination is most likely?
options: Less oxygen use and more ATP
More ATP with no heat production
No electron transport and more ATP
More oxygen use but less ATP
questions.explanation: Electron transport may accelerate while the gradient is dissipated as heat. Oxygen consumption can rise even though ATP production falls.
